title: Named Window Using the WINDOW Clause
description: For each order, show the order amount alongside the **regional total**, **regional average**, and **regional maximum** — all computed via window functions. Use a **named window** defined in a WINDOW clause to avoid repeating the partition expression three times.
solution_sql: SELECT order_id, region, amount, SUM(amount) OVER w AS region_total, ROUND(AVG(amount) OVER w, 2) AS region_avg, MAX(amount) OVER w AS region_max FROM orders WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY region) ORDER BY region, order_id

test_cases.description: 9 orders each with region_total, region_avg, region_max. North total=740, South total=665, East total=1025.

hints: Define the window once at the end of the query: WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY region), then reference it in each function as SUM(amount) OVER w.
The WINDOW clause is supported in PostgreSQL, MySQL 8+, and SQLite 3.25+ — it avoids repeating the same OVER (PARTITION BY region) three times.
explanation: The WINDOW clause (SQL:2003 standard) lets you name a window definition and reuse it across multiple functions. Here, w = PARTITION BY region, so SUM, AVG, and MAX all operate over the same partition without repetition. North: total=740, avg=246.67, max=310. South: total=665, avg=221.67, max=320. East: total=1025, avg=341.67, max=400.
